sections.title: Memes
sections.description: The July Meme of the Month results, kept in poll order and filtered to memes Lessons in Meme Culture covered in any upload from the past two months.

sources.label: Lessons in Meme Culture · past 2 months

items.title: Jimothy the raccoon
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: A round, short-spined Seattle raccoon celebrated through affectionate fan art, sighting posts, and jokes comparing compact objects to him.
items.alt: Visual example of the Jimothy the raccoon meme

items.title: Kwebbelkop Laugh
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: An exaggerated YourRAGE laugh paired with Kwebbelkop's face, used as an audio punchline and remixed into increasingly distorted reaction edits.
items.alt: Kwebbelkop portrait used with the viral laughing sound

items.title: Hatsune Miku World Cup Custody Battle
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: World Cup fans jokingly award “custody” of Hatsune Miku to each winning nation, then redraw her in that country's colors and culture.
items.alt: Visual example of the Hatsune Miku World Cup Custody Battle meme

items.title: Mbappé Special
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: From Kylian Mbappé calling his favorite thing to cook “nothing”; people now call an empty or nonexistent offering the “Mbappé Special.”
items.alt: Visual example of the Mbappé Special meme

items.title: John Rod
items.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
items.description: An unnamed JoJo stand nicknamed John Rod, used in absurd power-scaling jokes and fan edits that claim he can defeat anyone.
items.alt: John Rod from JoJo's Bizarre Adventure

moreItems.title: Stay In Character
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Stay In Character is a catchphrase and series of memes based on a scene from the 2026 Backrooms movie in which the protagonist, Clark (played by actor Chiwetel Ejiofor), yells, "Stay in character!" In June 2026, the film's scene became the subject of numerous memes on social media as the moment was used as an exploitable format with brainrot edits, recreations, Accuracy Reenactments and more.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Stay In Character meme

moreItems.title: Funky Ehh
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: We'll Drive A Funky Ehh or He'll Drive A Funky Ehh refers to a viral video of a kid claiming, during a game of Fortnite, that a remix of the song " Someone to Call My Lover " by Janet Jackson is by Oliver Tree, singing the song, "Maybe we'll meet at a bar, we'll drive a fancy ehh." A clip of the moment went viral on social media and Instagram Reels later that month, inspiring animations, remixes and memes based on the audio of the kid singing the song.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Funky Ehh meme

moreItems.title: Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here is a quote from the character Antinous, played by actor Robert Pattinson, in Christopher Nolan's 2026 epic fantasy movie The Odyssey, which appeared online shortly after the film's release in mid-July 2026. The scene is typically used online as a simple catchphrase and reaction meme to mock someone for being poor or begging for something, with the GIF or reaction image of Pattinson from the movie also being used as an exploitable in which creators add different visual elements to him.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Somebody Get These Beggars Out Of Here meme

moreItems.title: Homer Let the Barts Out
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Homer Let the Barts Out is a brainrot and AI song by Rabadoonga about Homer Simpson letting a massive group of Bart Simpsons out of the house, who go on to cause uncontrollable destruction. It inspired memes on sites including social media, X / Twitter and Instagram Reels, including lip dubs, animations, covers and AI-generated videos.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Homer Let the Barts Out meme

moreItems.title: Best of Zach
moreItems.subtitle: July poll finalist · LIMC covered
moreItems.description: Best Of Zach refers to a series of memes about the Oney Plays video "Best Of Zach" and its thumbnail, which shows a cartoon drawing of Zach, also known as PsychicPebbles, over a pink background. In June 2026, a video that animates the video and sets it to an amateur rap song that repeats the words "best of Zach" was popularized online, inspiring further "Best Of Zach" memes.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of the Best of Zach meme

sections.eyebrow: Annual slang review · by page views
sections.title: Slang
sections.description: Terms from Know Your Meme's annual slang review, ranked from most to least lifetime views on their Know Your Meme entries and checked against Urban Dictionary.

sources.label: Know Your Meme · annual slang review

items.title: 67 / six-seven
items.subtitle: A deliberately ambiguous number catchphrase
items.description: A call-and-response built around saying “six-seven,” often with a palms-up gesture. Its lack of one fixed meaning is the joke, so people use it as a deliberately contextless reply.
items.alt: The number 67 as used in the six-seven meme

items.title: Dead Rose Emoji
items.subtitle: The wilted rose used as ironic punctuation
items.description: The wilted rose emoji 🥀 became an ironic alternative to the broken-heart emoji. People append it to dramatic, embarrassing, disappointed, or mock-heartbroken remarks.
items.alt: Visual example of Dead Rose Emoji

items.title: Aura farming
items.subtitle: Performing effortless cool for status
items.description: Aura farming means doing something calculated to look effortlessly cool and build imaginary social status. The phrase captions dramatic entrances, poses, edits, and knowingly over-styled behavior.

items.title: SYBAU
items.subtitle: An aggressive request to be quiet
items.description: SYBAU expands to “shut your bitch ass up.” It is used as a blunt dismissal or exaggerated reaction, often as an acronym so the punchline lands only after someone decodes it.
items.alt: Reaction image associated with the acronym SYBAU

items.title: Labubu Matcha Dubai Chocolate
items.subtitle: A pileup of 2025 consumer-trend buzzwords
items.description: Labubu is a toothy collectible toy, matcha is a powdered green-tea drink, and Dubai chocolate is a pistachio-filled chocolate bar. Stringing them together parodies algorithm-driven consumer trends.
items.alt: Visual example of Labubu Matcha Dubai Chocolate

moreItems.title: Clanker
moreItems.subtitle: A derogatory word for robots
moreItems.description: A Star Wars insult for battle droids that returned as a joking slur for robots and AI. People use it to mock a machine, chatbot, or conspicuously automated behavior.
moreItems.alt: A battle droid associated with the slang term clanker

moreItems.title: TS PMO ICL
moreItems.subtitle: An intentionally overloaded slang acronym
moreItems.description: TS PMO ICL expands to “this shit pisses me off, I can’t lie.” People use it sincerely, or pile it into deliberately overloaded captions that parody compressed internet slang.
moreItems.alt: Visual example of TS PMO ICL

moreItems.title: Performative Male
moreItems.subtitle: Someone visibly curating an appealing persona
moreItems.description: A performative male conspicuously reads feminist books, drinks matcha, carries a tote bag, or wears wired earbuds to appear sensitive and attractive. The label mocks an obviously curated personality.

moreItems.title: Chopped
moreItems.subtitle: Unattractive, damaged, or badly done
moreItems.description: Calling someone or something “chopped” means it looks unattractive, damaged, or badly put together. It appears in blunt reactions, appearance jokes, and before-and-after comparisons.
moreItems.alt: Reaction image associated with chopped slang
